A working group on the taxation of leasing in favor of non-residents will be established under the Ministry of Finance
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
12:34:05 EEST
18:34:05 KST

A working group on the taxation of leasing in favor of non-residents will be established under the Ministry of Finance
Kyiv • UNN
The Tax Committee of the Public Council initiated a working group under the Ministry of Finance to analyze leasing payments to non-residents. The group will prepare a draft general tax consultation.
The Tax Committee of the Public Council under the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine proposed establishing a working group at the Ministry of Finance that would comprehensively analyze the taxation of leasing payments made to non-residents and develop a draft generalized tax consultation (GTC). The decision was made following the first meeting devoted to the problem of ambiguous interpretations of the relevant tax rules. Tetiana Shevtsova, a member of the Public Council under the Ministry of Finance, told UNN in a comment.
Details
As UNN reported earlier, the ESB is investigating cases involving at least five air carriers, including MAU, "Konstanta Airline," "Urga," H3Operations, and "Skyline Express," over the alleged failure to pay an additional 15% tax on income of non-residents to the Ukrainian budget under aircraft leasing agreements. Investigators equate leasing payments with royalties and treat airplanes and helicopters not as means of transport but as "equipment."
Law enforcement officers received the analytical findings after the previous State Tax Service team published an article in 2024 proposing that leasing operations involving transport owned by non-residents of Ukraine be taxed as royalties. The documents, which according to representatives of the aviation market are similar to one another and appear to have been written "from the same template," formed the basis for criminal cases against air carriers.
Lawyers interviewed by UNN point out that investigators are ignoring the applicable international conventions on the avoidance of double taxation ratified by the Verkhovna Rada. According to them, automatically assessing an additional 15% tax in Ukraine without taking into account the provisions of a specific convention is, at the very least, disputable.
It is worth noting that, according to the State Tax Service, the airlines underwent tax audits, and violations in the taxation of leasing were established based on only one of them. The remaining tax audits did not identify such violations.
Representatives of Ukraine's aviation industry stated that civil aviation is at risk of destruction due to the actions of state regulatory authorities. According to them, the new interpretation of the taxation of aircraft leasing operations involving non-residents of Ukraine as royalties, criminal proceedings, and attempts to assess additional taxes for seven years could ultimately finish off companies that survived the closure of the airspace and relocation abroad due to the full-scale war
The Ministry of Finance will comprehensively examine the issue of aviation leasing
According to Tetiana Shevtsova, the issue of taxing leasing payments was submitted for consideration by the Tax Committee of the Public Council under the Ministry of Finance following a corresponding appeal from the Ukrainian Air Transport Association. Specialists from the relevant departments of the Ministry of Finance, representatives of associations, and members of the Public Council's Tax Committee took part in the meeting.
Following consideration of the association's appeal, the meeting of the Tax Committee of the Public Council under the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine considered the issue of taxing rental payments made to non-residents
According to Shevtsova, the meeting's participants unanimously agreed that the issue required a comprehensive analysis, taking into account not only the provisions of Ukrainian tax legislation but also international law.
They unanimously reached a decision on the need for a comprehensive examination of the issue raised, both from the standpoint of the definitions in the Tax Code of Ukraine and of International Agreements (Conventions) on the avoidance of double taxation and the OECD and UN Model Conventions
A working group is proposed to be established at the Ministry of Finance
At the same time, the problem extends beyond the aviation industry alone, since the approach to classifying rental payments made to non-residents also concerns other sectors of the economy. It is known that similar problems arose during the leasing of railway cars and agricultural machinery. That is why the Public Council's Tax Committee took the initiative to establish a special working group at the Ministry of Finance.
Also, given the relevance of the issue both to the aviation industry and to other sectors, the Tax Committee of the Public Council under the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine (the Ministry of Finance of Ukraine — ed.) took the initiative to establish a working group under the Ministry of Finance to develop a draft General Tax Consultation, with the involvement of representatives of the Public Council, the Ministry of Finance, and the State Tax Service
It is expected that the working group itself will thoroughly examine the legal grounds for taxing lease payments to nonresidents and prepare a draft General Tax Consultation. After that, the document is to be submitted for consideration by the Expert Council under the Ministry of Finance.
The General Tax Consultation could become a mechanism for establishing a unified approach by government authorities to the taxation of such transactions and eliminating differing interpretations of tax regulations, including by investigators of the Economic Security Bureau.
Initiating criminal prosecution against air carriers on the basis of a disputed interpretation of tax regulations, before the fact of a violation has been conclusively established, raises serious legal questions and places unjustified pressure on businesses.

In 5 questions:  Why Trump renames Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:33:17 UTC
18:33:17 KST

- Move adds symbolic friction to strained US-Canada ties after collapse of trade talks and imposition of new tariffs
 
US President Donald Trump on Thursday signed an executive order directing his administration to refer to Lake Ontario as “Lake America,” adding a symbolic point of friction to already strained relations between Washington and Ottawa.
The move comes after three days of trade negotiations collapsed last week and the US imposed 50% tariffs on about $20 billion worth of Canadian goods.
Canada responded with tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on C$27.6 billion ($20 billion) worth of US imports. The measures, covering about 700 products, are due to take effect Sept. 8.
 
Why did Trump rename the lake?
Trump first raised the possibility of changing the Great Lake’s name on Tuesday, saying the US was considering the move because it did not expect to be “doing much business with Ontario any longer.”
Trump has long accused Canada of taking advantage of the US on trade and defense, but said the change was not intended to send a specific geopolitical message.
The executive order presents the US as the principal protector of the Great Lakes and emphasizes Lake Ontario’s role in American commerce and history.
It says the lake’s deepest waters and most of its volume are within US territory. While shared between the two countries, however, a slim majority of about 52% of the lake’s surface area on the Canadian side.
 
What is Lake Ontario and where does its name come from?
Lake Ontario, bordered by the Canadian province of Ontario and the US state of New York, is the smallest and easternmost of North America’s five Great Lakes.
Its waters flow into the St. Lawrence River, forming part of a commercial route connecting the North American interior with the Atlantic Ocean.
The lake’s name has Indigenous origins and is generally traced to the Iroquoian term “oniatari:io,” commonly translated as “lake of shining waters,” though other interpretations include “beautiful lake” and “great lake.”
The name predates both the US and modern Canada. The province of Ontario, established in 1867, later took its name from the lake.
Lake Ontario also had strategic importance during the War of 1812, when Britain and the US built rival naval forces on it to control military supply routes.
 
Why is the lake important today?
Lake Ontario remains economically and environmentally significant to both countries.
It supports major population centers, industry, commercial shipping, fisheries, recreation and tourism.
Its location at the eastern end of the Great Lakes system also makes it a key link between the North American interior and the Atlantic Ocean through the St. Lawrence Seaway.
Because the lake is shared, the US and Canada cooperate on navigation, water levels, fisheries, water quality and environmental protection.
Their management of shared waters is governed in part by the 1909 Boundary Waters Treaty, which established the International Joint Commission to help prevent and resolve transboundary disputes.
 
Does Trump have authority to change the name?
The executive order can determine how the US federal government refers to the lake, but it cannot require Canada to use the name “Lake America.”
Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly said Canada would “always call it Lake Ontario,” while Ontario Premier Doug Ford dismissed the proposal as “a lot of rhetoric.”
The US Board on Geographic Names, which operates under the Interior Department, standardizes geographic names for use by the federal government.
Trump’s order directs Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to update federal maps, documents and databases within 30 days.
The order does not affect Canadian naming practices, and there is no international authority that can impose a single name for a body of water shared by two countries.
As a result, US federal records could use “Lake America” while Canada and other countries continue to refer to the same body as Lake Ontario.
 
Why does the renaming matter?
The immediate practical effect of Trump’s move is largely confined to US federal usage, but it carries political significance amid fraying US-Canada relations.
In response, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the change, saying: “Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario – then, now and always.”
It is not the first time Trump has used geographic naming changes to emphasize what his administration describes as American heritage and national identity.
A similar naming controversy followed Trump’s decision to rename the Gulf of Mexico the “Gulf of America” for US federal use.
The move, announced early in his second term, has been rejected by Mexico, which continues to use the Gulf of Mexico.
Trump’s latest order does not alter the international boundary or existing arrangements for jointly managing the lake, but it adds another dispute to increasingly strained relations between Washington and Ottawa.

Nepal and China briefly halt rescue efforts as barrier lake overflows
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:30:45 UTC
18:30:45 KST

Nepal and China briefly halt rescue efforts as barrier lake overflows
More than 580 people dead and more than 2,400 missing after the flash flood disaster that struck on Wednesday.
Nepal and China have resumed rescue efforts for survivors of the devastating flash flood that hit the border region two days ago, following a brief suspension as a “barrier lake” formed during the disaster began to overflow.
Chinese rescue teams and vehicles were forced to pull back to safe ground, state broadcaster CCTV reported, as the risk of the lake bursting rose. Nepalese authorities also paused search operations for 90 minutes, an army officer confirmed on Friday.
“As the risk posed by the upstream dammed lake was deemed manageable, rescue operations for the Gyirong mudslide disaster quickly resumed and were stepped up,” CCTV said.
Nepal’s army spokesperson said the rise in water level comprised just 0.6 metres (two feet).
Rescuers earlier feared the “barrier lake”, formed as Wednesday’s flash flood carried huge volumes of mud and debris down a steep valley, could unleash another huge and destructive wave.
In Nepal’s Rasuwa district, on the border with Tibet, residents were seen scrambling up hillsides to escape potential surges in the river level, according to the Reuters news agency.
The disaster unfolded as a glacier collapsed and sent a huge torrent of ice, water, rock, and mud down Himalayan river valleys, burying entire villages and destroying roads, bridges, and hydropower plants.
In its wake, leftover debris trapped water to form a barrier lake, a natural dam created when landslides block a river.
With water continuing to pour into the lake, the threat to downstream communities of another wave of flooding rose. China deployed an engineering team to conduct aerial surveys and 3D modelling of the site.
By Friday afternoon, however, the secondary flood scare was confirmed to be “nowhere near” the magnitude of Wednesday’s disaster, said David Fisher, the delegation head for the Nepal International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC).
The lake overflow added to “ongoing terror” rocking communities who have lost their homes, finding refuge in schools and government buildings, Fisher told Al Jazeera.
“It’s an extremely difficult time,” he added.
Relief supplies blocked
The death toll from the disaster continues to rise. On Friday, Nepal’s disaster authority reported at least 579 deaths, with 1,924 people missing.
Chinese authorities reported on Friday that the death toll in Tibet has now risen to at least five, with 558 people missing.
Bishal Nath Upreti, president of the Nepal Centre for Disaster Management, told Al Jazeera that conditions are “extremely difficult” for those trapped in the disaster zone, as destroyed roads have left them completely cut off.
Nepal’s disaster authority said a total of 4,451 people had been rescued as of Friday, with 16 helicopters carrying out 99 rescue flights so far.
Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Beijing, said the number of missing is expected to rise. China has deployed about 500 military and paramilitary personnel and sent Premier Li Qiang to supervise operations on the ground, while Nepal has deployed 30,000 security personnel to search remote, cut-off valleys, she said.
More than 90,000 people are estimated to have been affected by disaster, the IRFC’s Fisher said on Friday.
Teams have been unable to reach some of the hardest-hit areas in Rasuwa, which remains accessible only via helicopter.
“We’re very concerned for them,” Fisher said.

South Korea cleared for 103 AIM-9X missiles
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
10:30:42 BST
18:30:42 KST

The United States has approved a possible $125 million Foreign Military Sale to South Korea covering 103 AIM-9X Sidewinder Block II air-to-air missiles, additional guidance units and associated support, the UK Defence Journal understands.
The US Department of State announced the determination on 21 August under Foreign Military Sales transmittal 26-78. The package requested by the Republic of Korea includes 103 AIM-9X Sidewinder Block II tactical missiles and ten AIM-9X Block II Tactical Guidance Units.
Associated equipment and services would include active optical target detectors, training, weapon-system support, training aids and devices, spare parts and US Government and contractor engineering, technical and logistics support.
The estimated value of the complete package is $125 million. As with other Foreign Military Sales notifications, the figure represents the estimated value of the proposed programme rather than necessarily the value of any eventual contract.
The State Department said the proposed sale would support US foreign policy and national security objectives through South Korea’s role as an American ally in the Indo-Pacific. It also said the weapons would expand the country’s air-defence capability and support interoperability with US forces.
In its notification, the department stated that the sale would “help improve the Republic of Korea’s capability to meet current and future threats by expanding its air defense capability, deterring aggression in the region, and ensuring interoperability with U.S. Forces.”
It added: “The Republic of Korea will have no difficulty absorbing these articles and services into its armed forces.”
The AIM-9X is the current generation of the Sidewinder family of short-range infrared-guided air-to-air missiles used by the United States and a number of allied air forces. The Block II version incorporates updated guidance and electronics compared with earlier variants and is designed for employment from compatible fighter aircraft using both traditional and high-off-boresight engagements.
South Korea already operates a substantial fleet of US-designed combat aircraft, including the F-15K Slam Eagle, KF-16 and F-35A Lightning II, alongside domestically developed types. The country continues to modernise its combat-air inventory while maintaining close operational links with US forces stationed on the Korean Peninsula and elsewhere in the region.
The principal contractor identified for the proposed sale is RTX Corporation, headquartered in Arlington, Virginia. The State Department said it was not currently aware of any offset agreement associated with the potential programme, with any such arrangement to be determined separately between the purchaser and contractor.

Kraków withdraws fireworks ban after negative court ruling

A ban on the use of fireworks that was introduced last year by Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city, has been withdrawn after the local authorities decided not to appeal against a court decision revoking it.
Kraków had argued that the ban would boost the safety and health of both humans and animals. However, opponents of the measures, including the provincial governor, who launched the legal challenge against it, argued that it was excessive and undermined constitutional freedoms.
Kraków bez zakazu fajerwerków. Miasto nie zaskarży wyroku WSAhttps://t.co/rPEYNhEMAQ
— Fakty RMF FM (@RMF24pl) August 25, 2026
In November 2025, Kraków’s city council adopted a resolution banning fireworks, firecrackers, sparklers and other pyrotechnic materials being set off “for entertainment purposes”.
The ban, which carried an exemption for last year’s New Year’s celebrations, applied in public spaces as well as private properties where the use of fireworks was deemed to impact public places.
The city said the ban aimed to “protect the life, health and peace of residents” and “ensure public safety”, adding that the discharge of pyrotechnics created noise and air pollution and could pose a threat to the health and life of humans and animals.
Some councillors also argued that a ban would benefit residents suffering from trauma, including World War Two veterans and Ukrainian refugees. The city’s then mayor, Aleksander Miszalski, cited a city poll finding that 67.5% of respondents supported a year-round ban on fireworks and 31.2% opposed it.
However, the measures were criticised by the head of the Association of Pyrotechnic Importers and Distributors, Marta Smolińska, who told news service Puls Krakowa that the ban was an “extreme solution” that would hurt local businesses. She called instead for “promoting the responsible use of pyrotechnics”.
In December, Krzysztof Klęczar, the government-appointed governor of the Małopolska province, of which Kraków is the capital, announced that he would challenge the ban in the Provincial Administrative Court.
Klęczar argued that the measures may “violate the principle of proportionality of limiting constitutional freedoms and rights as well as the freedom…to conduct business activity”.
National parks in Poland have appealed to revellers to refrain from using fireworks this New Year’s Eve to avoid awakening wild animals from their winter slumber.
A number of cities have also called on residents to abandon the tradition to protect petshttps://t.co/T6RQHdsF9P
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 29, 2022
His arguments were endorsed by the court, which, in a ruling in late June, deemed the resolution introducing the ban “invalid” and ordered that the city of Kraków pay legal costs.
The court said the ban “went beyond the competence of the city council” and “violated the principle of proportionality of the protection of constitutional freedoms and rights”. It added that it “was not necessary to protect health, life or public order”.
While Kraków could have appealed against the ruling at the Supreme Administrative Court, it has decided not to take that step. An appeal “would probably have little chance of upholding the resolution,” spokeswoman Dominika Jaźwiecka-Bujalska told the Polish Press Agency (PAP).
Poland's largest opposition group has proposed a law banning fireworks, arguing that they cause distress, and even death, among domestic pets and wild animals https://t.co/UVzFMv3IEn
— Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 23, 2021
At the national level, in 2021, Civic Coalition (KO) – which was then the largest opposition party and is now Poland’s main ruling party – proposed a law that would have banned the use of most fireworks and firecrackers to protect domestic and wild animals.
While that legislation did not proceed beyond a parliamentary commission, two further bills seeking to limit the use of fireworks to protect animals are currently proceeding in parliament, reports local news service Portal Samorządowy.
Several Polish cities have introduced their own restrictions, which in some cases have also faced legal challenges. Wrocław, Poland’s third-largest city, also introduced a ban in January, which was likewise revoked in an administrative court after facing opposition from the provincial governor, reports PAP.
Year-round bans remain in place in the Baltic resort town of Sopot, where there is an exemption for 31 December and 1 January, and the southern mountain resort town of Zakopane, a popular destination for New Year’s revellers, where the New Year period is included.

There Are So Many Conspiracy Theories About Dolly Parton and Vaccines
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:30:00 UTC
18:30:00 KST

Conspiracy theories surrounding singer and philanthropist Dolly Parton’s recent death have flooded the internet, referencing everything from satanic rituals to cloning. But one conspiracy theory has dominated all the others: the claim that Parton’s death was caused by “turbo cancer” brought on by the Covid vaccine.
There is no evidence to support the claim that Parton’s death had anything to do with the vaccine. Parton, 80, died after “a short battle with cancer,” her family said in a statement. In May, Parton shared that she was responding well to treatment related to her immune system and digestive system.
In 2020, the singer donated $1 million to fund research in support of the vaccine. The following year, she filmed herself getting the vaccine, singing an adapted version of her hit song Jolene before receiving the shot. “Vaccine, vaccine, vaccine, vaccine, I'm begging of you, please don't hesitate," Parton sang in a video.
Now, a number of influential right-wing conspiracy theorists and MAGA-aligned pundits have spent the past few days claiming—or, in many cases, suggesting—that the vaccine killed Parton.
“Was Dolly Parton yet another Covid vaccine victim?” far-right radio host Wayne Allyn Root, who recently interviewed President Donald Trump on his show, wrote on X. "She took the vaxx on TV. She changed the name of her hit song 'Jolene Jolene' to 'Vaccine, Vaccine.' She encouraged fans to get it. Now she's dead of cancer. This sounds like another case of 'turbo cancer. RIP Dolly.” (Earlier this month, Root urged Trump to declare a national emergency during the midterms when he had the president on his show. “Let me just say, stranger things have happened, OK?” Trump responded.)
“Dolly Parton thought she was doing the right thing by backing the Moderna mRNA Covid shot,” Toby Rogers, who works with the Brownstone Institute, a think tank founded to oppose Covid restrictions and which has deep ties to the Trump administration, wrote on X. “But it very well may have killed her.” The Brownstone Institute was founded by Jeffrey Tucker, a close ally of Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who has long undermined trust in a variety of vaccines.
While Kennedy has not commented publicly on Parton’s death, he has spent recent days blaming the Covid lockdowns for measles-related deaths, after the measles-related deaths of two unvaccinated people in Pennsylvania this week.
Valerie Anne Smith, a health influencer with 273,000 followers on X, shared multiple posts about Parton’s death, all of them suggesting that the Covid-19 vaccine was the cause of her death.
“Soon after being injected she developed severe autoimmune, liver and kidney issues,” Smith wrote. “Cause of death ... CANCER.”
“Dolly Parton was as universally beloved as a person can be,” Travis View, cohost of the QAnon Anonymous podcast, tells WIRED. “That’s exactly what made her a target for conspiracists online. Many anti-vaccine conspiracy theorists despised Parton because she not only encouraged others to get the vaccine, she even helped fund vaccine development.”
The conspiracy theories were not limited to X. Facebook was also flooded with wild allegations about Parton’s death, none of which provided any evidence to back up their claims.
One of the most popular themes focused on a video Parton made just weeks before her death in which she thanked pop star Taylor Swift and her husband, NFL star Travis Kelce, for their $2 million donation to Imagination Library, Parton’s childhood literacy charity. She jokingly also asked the couple if she could have their “firstborn” child.
The conspiracy theories focused on a brief moment in the video when Parton was moving her hands. Some social media users claimed that if paused, the video showed her making a “devil horns,” sign. The still image has been posted dozens of times on Facebook in recent days, garnering tens of thousands of likes and shares.
“Nothing to see here, folks, just Dolly Parton—the same woman who dropped $1 million to help fund the Moderna Covid vaccine—flashing devil horns while casually demanding Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s firstborn child,” an anonymous X account named Red Pill USA wrote, adding: “It’s a big Satanic club … and you ain’t in it.” The post has been viewed almost 1 million times.
On YouTube, conspiracy theorist David Nino Rodriguez, who has 613,000 followers, also referenced the Taylor Swift video and dedicated his show on Wednesday to claims that Parton’s death had been prophesied, and that it was a “marker for what comes next.”
“Some of these theories came specifically from her advocacy for the Covid vaccine and gay rights, and they're pretty rare when balanced with the outpouring of love,” Mike Rothschild, an author who writes about conspiracy theories, tells WIRED. “But a lot of what was said about Dolly was just standard-issue brain rot. There is a small part of the internet that now believes nobody dies without some involvement from the Covid vaccine, trafficking, or Satanism.”

Serbia says war criminal Mladic to be buried with 'state honors'
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:28:00 UTC
18:28:00 KST

Convicted war criminal Ratko Mladic, whose forces besieged the Bosnian capital for several years in the 1990s and carried out the worst massacre in Europe since World War II, "will receive all the military and state honors to which he is entitled," Serbia said Friday.
Mladic died Thursday while serving a life sentence in The Hague for war crimes committed during the 1990s Bosnian war. He was 84.
"It is certain that General Mladic will receive all the military and state honours to which he is entitled, as far as the state is concerned," Serbia's Justice Minister Nenad Vujic said.
Serbian officials were awaiting details on when authorities in The Hague would release the body, he told the K1 broadcaster.
"We are ready to leave for The Hague as soon as we learn what the next steps are," the minister said.
Mladic, who had suffered several strokes in recent months, was serving a life sentence for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity during the Bosnian War, including for his role in the Srebrenica massacre, Europe's worst act of bloodshed since World War II.
His conviction in 2017 for the wartime killings was considered a key step toward bringing justice to the victims and led the international press to dub him the "Butcher of Bosnia."
He had been in custody since 2011 after many years on the run.
The ruthless, former communist officer-turned nationalist warlord was one of the most notorious figures of the Bosnian War that left more than 100,000 people dead and over 1 million homeless. He commanded his troops to "scorch the brains" of the Bosnian Muslims and boasted of being a "Serbian God."
The Hague tribunal said at the time the crimes committed were "amongst the most heinous known to humankind." Former U.N. rights chief Zeid Ra'ad al Hussein described him as "the epitome of evil."
Mladic was the military face of a brutal trio, led on the political side by ex-Yugoslav president Slobodan Milosevic and former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic. Milosevic also died in the custody of the Hague court in 2006 while on trial for genocide.
When the ethnic war in Bosnia-Herzegovina started in 1992, Mladic became the commander of the Bosnian Serb troops and took control of large swaths of the country to form a Serb mini-state.
Serbs under Mladic's control laid siege to the Bosnian capital, Sarajevo, and other cities and villages, established concentration camps for detained non-Serb civilians and enemy soldiers, and systematically killed prisoners. In Sarajevo, Serb troops kept the city isolated while killing civilians with snipers and heavy artillery.
In 1995, Mladic's troops slaughtered more than 8,000 Muslim men and boys in Srebrenica – the first case of genocide in Europe since WWII.
To this day, many Serbs still see him as a hero. Local authorities in Bosnia's Serb entity, Republika Srpska, called on residents to pay their respects to Mladic in churches across the entity.

Estonia averages nearly 100 traffic collisions a day
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:23:00 UTC
18:23:00 KST

Estonia averages nearly 100 traffic collisions a day
While crashes involving injuries fell, Estonia recorded nearly 100 traffic insurance claims a day in the first half of 2026, up 14 percent from the same period last year.
The Estonian Motor Insurance Bureau (LKF) reported 17,851 claims in the first six months of this year, averaging 99 a day, with the Jüri junction on Tallinn Ring Road again the country's most collision-prone location.
"An average of 99 traffic insurance claims a day means one incident occurs roughly every 15 minutes," LKF board chair Tuuli Pärenson said.
Behind every incident, she stressed, are people facing at least unexpected paperwork and, in the worst cases, injuries and other long-term consequences.
Meanwhile, the Police and Border Guard Board (PPA) reported 5 percent fewer crashes involving injuries. There were 687 such collisions nationwide in the first half of the year, killing 22 people and injuring 849.
Taavi Kirss, head of traffic enforcement at the PPA, said the decline was encouraging but not enough.
"A driver who runs a red light or repeatedly overtakes [other vehicles] on the highway should understand that in that moment, they themselves are the greatest danger on the road," he said, stressing that such bad habits need to change in order to keep others safe.
Parking lots frequent collision site
Over the past 12 months, the Jüri junction in Rae Municipality was the incident site for 135 insurance claims worth a total of €360,000 in damage, followed by Tallinn's Ülemiste junction with 111 claims and €328,000 in damage and the Sõpruse puiestee–Tammsaare tee intersection with 101 claims.
More than 40 percent of all collisions prompting traffic insurance claims occur in parking lots.
Three major shopping mall parking lots accounted for the most claims over the past year, with 163 claims filed for incidents in Tallinn's Ülemste Center, 100 for Tartu's Lõunakeskus and 78 for Tallinn's Rocca al Mare Center.

It ain’t pretty: botched Botox on the rise in country’s youth
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:22:46 UTC
18:22:46 KST

It ain’t pretty: botched Botox on the rise in country’s youth
See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results
Just as the new school year gets underway, the Dutch Health and Youth Care Inspectorate (IGJ) has warned about a five-fold increase in complaints resulting from failed cosmetic treatments involving Botox and other dermal fillers.
The IGC received 175 reports of failed treatments, up from some 35 per year in the preceding years. The skyrocketing numbers, they say, are largely due to increased demand for the procedures among youth looking for fuller lips and less wrinkles and a surge in places providing them.
Young people, IGJ inspector Rosemarie Jansen told broadcaster NOS, were especially vulnerable to cutthroat rates among providers who often lack the mandatory qualifications to provide them. That “lowers the threshold for young people, precisely because they do not have much to spend,” she said.
Some 67% of the complaints involved a practitioner who was not legally qualified or lacked the necessary medical competence.
In the Netherlands, a doctor is required to be present when a patient receives such cosmetic treatments, something which is lacking in the proliferation of places offering them.
The botched procedures have led to swelling and drooping eyelids, lip inflammation and allergic reactions. The ICJ says the number of complaints is likely unreported due to the shame many young people feel about getting cosmetic work.
Fillercheck.nl
To help combat the problem, the IGC, along with Tilburg University and the consumer platform wiemooiwilzijn, have created fillercheck.nl, a website where those seeking cosmetic treatments can go down a four-part checklist that gets them thinking about the treatment, lets them find out if their provider is qualified and, says the IGC, help them recognize red flags.
The Inspectorate is taking their message via pop-up clinics disguised as cosmetic treatment centres to students in Amsterdam, Nijmegen, Zwolle and Breda this week and next – just in time for university introduction weeks.

Mucahithan Avcioglu
28 August 2026•Update: 28 August 2026
Germany's unemployed population remained above 3 million in August as labor market stagnation persisted despite recent positive economic signals, official data showed Friday.
The number of unemployed people rose by 54,000 from July and by 36,000 from a year earlier to 3.061 million, according to the Federal Employment Agency.
The unemployment rate increased to 6.5% from 6.4% in July.
Federal Employment Agency Chairwoman Andrea Nahles said the labor market showed no notable momentum in August beyond the usual seasonal effects.
Germany's unemployed population exceeded 3 million in July for the first time since April, partly due to the start of the summer holiday period.
Economists said the steady rise in unemployment since July reflected both seasonal factors and the economy's cyclical weakness.
Recent signs of improving economic activity, however, are expected to support the labor market in the coming period.

The Palestinian Circus takes flight despite Israeli occupation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:20:51 UTC
18:20:51 KST

Breadcrumb
For The Palestinian Circus, the sky, not occupation, is the limit
It might be a grey and wet afternoon in Edinburgh, but wind-assisted rain is no force powerful enough to dampen the spirits of The Palestinian Circus, a troupe of artists from across Palestine performing at the Scottish capital's Festival Fringe.
In a circus tent on the city's muddied Meadows, the group performs hoop work, juggling, acrobatics, Chinese pole, trapeze, silk straps, LED lighting and fireworks, blended with Palestinian dabke folk dance.
This novel and breathtaking blend of disciplines first saw the light of day after the group was invited to perform at Glastonbury Festival last year.
"The artists chose and started to work on how to blend circus techniques and disciplines with dabke, to celebrate Palestinian identity, culture, hope, and resistance," The Palestinian Circus's artistic director, Noor Abo Alrob, tells The New Arab about the show, The Palestinian Circus: Step and a Half.
"After Glastonbury, we said we wanted to develop the idea further and create a full show about this concept."
The creation of this full show began in May, but bringing performers from cities in the occupied West Bank and Jerusalem together to develop it was difficult on a daily basis, Noor shares.
"Some days, it wasn’t easy for the artists to go home. On other days, it was really challenging for them to come in, so we needed to postpone some of the training. We also couldn't do it for days in a row where everyone could come and sleep in the same space. But we did our best."
Circus with a purpose
The Palestinian Circus was established 20 years ago by Palestinian actor and theatre teacher Shadi Zmorrod and Belgian social worker Jessika Devlieghere. At the time, the circus was very much a foreign concept in Palestine, Noor says.
"Before 2006, performers would come from different countries to Palestine and give workshops," he says.
"The idea was to establish something Palestinian, with Palestinian staff and team, for the Palestinian children – that was the starting point for it."
The circus operates on two pathways, Noor explains – one artistic, training young Palestinian circus artists, and the other social.
"With the social programmes, the idea is to spread circus in Palestine, and give every Palestinian child the chance to at least be part of the circus," he continues.
"We believe circus is for everyone, everywhere – in the West Bank, in Gaza, in Jerusalem – wherever Palestinians are. The focus is on bringing people together, building a community, and letting them think together and share something together."
The artistic group "creates and tours circus shows everywhere in Palestine that we can reach – villages, refugee camps, cities, schools, everywhere."
Performers in the artistic programme use show creation to express themselves on Palestinian social and political issues, which, Noor says, is particularly necessary when Palestinians are so often misrepresented internationally.
"Usually when we create a show, the artist does research, and they choose to talk about power, or gender issues in Palestinian society, or Israeli occupation – or Palestinian identity, like the show we are here with today."
The result is a defiant and, at most times, joyous show, broken up by segments of dabke that compel us to clap along; our claps move from rhythmic, excited, responsive flurries to, at times, jaw-dropping circus stunts. One performer falls metres from the Chinese pole into the arms of her troupe, to the echoing, reverberating sound of statements like: "Every fall teaches me a lesson."
Noor notes, "The circus and the show require a lot of coordination, communication, teamwork and trust. If the person who is falling does not have one hundred percent, blind trust that they will fall and the group will catch them, and if there is no eye communication between the group and the person falling, the trick will not work, and someone will be injured – or maybe even die, if they are falling from three or four metres high."
A lot of those values – communication, teamwork, trust – are a key part of the circus's social programme too, which has reached thousands of children in Jerusalem, the West Bank and Gaza, according to Noor.
Overcoming obstacles
The Palestinian Circus has always had to respond to the challenges of operating under Israeli occupation, but matters have become worse since Israel's genocide in Gaza began, as well as with its tightening stranglehold on the West Bank.
"During the genocide in Gaza, most of the circus artists have lost their houses and their family members, and some of them have been killed too," Noor highlights.
"In the past two to three years, we have not been able to plan anything long-term because things keep changing. Sometimes the checkpoints are closed in the West Bank, so we need to postpone shows and training, and cancel events… It's getting worse, and it’s getting harder to move between cities."
These cruel conditions have not kept the circus down; instead, its team has developed new strategies on how to overcome them, including a new training programme for those with basic circus knowledge who want to teach circus in their local community.
"We're trying to build a more sustainable model so that people who teach are from the same area as the students, and so that if we can’t reach that city, the training or shows or activities can still happen," Noor explains.
Taking the magic further
The circus is not just doubling down in the face of adversity, but quadrupling down. The team currently has one circus tent for shows, based in Birzeit, but by September, it will have four across the West Bank.
These tents will allow more circus artists to train at the heights they need for aerial arts, and will allow the magic of the circus to reach even more Palestinians.
"The idea is to have one of these circus tents be mobile, so we can take the full circus experience somewhere and leave it there for perhaps three months, to do shows and training for the community," Noor says.
"We'll be able to take the full circus experience to the communities that have not had the chance to see any art or circus shows before."
From the thousands of artists and shows at the Edinburgh Fringe, these artists will bring new inspiration back to Palestine once the festival is over.
"It's a really amazing opportunity," Noor says. "Being part of such a big festival, you really get to connect to people from all over the world… even Palestinians in the diaspora whom we don't or can't meet in Palestine."

Explainer: What challenges await rescuers in China's Xizang border mudslide?
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
17:19:42 CST
18:19:42 KST

GYIRONG, Xizang, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Rescue forces have been quickly deployed to a mudslide-hit port along the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, but relief operations remain severely hampered by complex and dangerous conditions on the ground.
Official figures show that a fast-moving chain mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse on the Nepalese side, swept through Gyirong Port on Wednesday morning. The disaster has left five people dead and 558 others missing, including 260 foreign nationals.
Xinhua reporters at the scene said the mudslide has devastated the river valley below. The silt layer in the core disaster area is more than 1.5 meters deep, posing a high risk of trapping anyone caught in it.
Chinese rescue teams mobilized swiftly to the remote mountainous border region. The first contingent of 141 emergency rescuers reached Gyirong Port on Thursday morning. Another 111 members of China's national search and rescue team arrived in Gyirong County by 2:28 p.m. Thursday.
The People's Liberation Army Xizang Military Command has deployed two batches of military helicopters to conduct aerial assessments, map rescue flight routes and carry out intensive searches, while also ferrying medical and rescue equipment to the affected area.
Despite these efforts, rescuers on site say operations are extremely challenging due to several factors.
The first is the risk of secondary disasters. The meteorological department forecasts light to moderate rain or thunderstorms across most of Gyirong County from Wednesday night to Sunday, with heavy rain in some southern low-altitude towns. These downpours could trigger flash floods, mudslides and landslides in vulnerable areas, potentially disrupting rescue work.
The county authorities have also warned that a barrier lake, formed upstream of the port by the glacier collapse, sits in an unstable geological setting and could breach, endangering rescue operations downstream.
The second obstacle is damaged road infrastructure. Local authorities said a road about three kilometers from the site was destroyed by the mudslide, delaying rescue access and slowing response efforts.
The third challenge is the temporary loss of contact with the disaster zone. In the immediate aftermath, communications and power supply were cut off, leaving the situation in the core area unknown for a time.
By around 4 p.m. Thursday, communication signals were restored in a village three kilometers from the port, marking phased progress in emergency communication support, authorities said.
The National Commission for Disaster Prevention, Reduction and Relief, together with the Ministry of Emergency Management (MEM), helped allocate 30,000 central relief supplies, including tents, stoves, clothing, quilts, folding beds and moisture-proof mats, to support evacuation, resettlement and relief work.
The Ministry of Finance and the MEM also allocated 120 million yuan (about 17.7 million U.S. dollars) in central natural disaster relief funds to support Xizang in carrying out emergency rescue and disaster relief operations.
Governments at all levels in Xizang and relevant departments have promptly organized disaster prevention efforts and risk avoidance measures, and have properly relocated and resettled those under threat.
A total of 499 villagers and construction workers have been properly accommodated. Meanwhile, 555 affected tourists were evacuated and transferred under the coordination of cultural and tourism authorities. No tourists remain stranded. ■

The Cabinet of Ministers approved a strategy to combat gambling addiction through 2035
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
12:19:41 EEST
18:19:41 KST

The Cabinet of Ministers approved a strategy to combat gambling addiction through 2035
Kyiv • UNN
The strategy will bring together around 40 government agencies and provides for prevention, early detection, and assistance for people with gambling addiction.
The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine has adopted a comprehensive state plan to combat gambling addiction, designed to run until 2035. It concerns the Strategy for Combating Gambling Addiction, reports the State Agency of Ukraine PlayCity, as reported by UNN.
Details
According to the Cabinet resolution No. 855-r of August 26, 2026, "the high level of psycho-emotional stress caused by the prolonged armed aggression of the russian federation against Ukraine significantly increases the propensity for gambling as a destructive way of coping with stress, which raises the risk of developing gambling addiction (ludomania)." In particular, this occurs among such potentially vulnerable population groups as military personnel, war veterans, and people facing difficult life circumstances.
Young people constitute a particularly high-risk group, in particular young people who are not studying or working, are outside the formal education system, and are facing difficult life circumstances as a result of the armed aggression of the russian federation against Ukraine
This strategy brings together the work of around 40 government agencies and covers the full range of measures - from preventing and early identifying the risks of gambling addiction to helping people who have already encountered it.
To remind you
The Cabinet of Ministers dismissed Hennadii Novikov from the position of head of the PlayCity agency, which regulates gambling in Ukraine. Novikov's deputy, Oleksii Tomashuk, will head the agency instead.

El Nino swings wider than in past 1,000 years, coral record shows
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
17:19:40 CST
18:19:40 KST

LOS ANGELES, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- El Nino-related temperature swings in the Pacific have become stronger than at any point measured in the preindustrial portion of a roughly 1,000-year record, a new study published Thursday in the journal Science has found.
The findings add to evidence that global warming may be changing the El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a natural climate cycle that affects weather around the world.
The study found that ENSO variability in recent decades was more than 36 percent higher than during the preindustrial period, with the strongest increase occurring over roughly the past 40 years.
ENSO includes the warm El Nino phase and the cold La Nina phase. Both can shift rainfall and temperatures far beyond the Pacific, affecting drought, floods and agriculture in many parts of the world, the study said.
The recent increase was largely driven by more frequent and stronger El Nino events. The change also paralleled the rise in global temperatures, it added.
The findings come as a new El Nino develops in the tropical Pacific. The U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's climate prediction center said on Aug. 13 that El Nino was strengthening, with a greater than 90 percent chance of a very strong event during the Northern Hemisphere fall and winter of 2026-27.
The new Science study does not indicate that every future El Nino will be stronger. It said, however, that recent eastern Pacific ENSO variability exceeds the range found in the preindustrial centuries covered by the coral record. ■

Multi-pronged rescue efforts under way after fatal mudslide hits China's Xizang border
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
17:19:37 CST
18:19:37 KST

This photo taken on Aug. 28, 2026 shows rescue operations underway at the mudslide-hit area. Emergency rescue operations have been carried out in an orderly and well-coordinated manner after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port in Gyirong County, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Wednesday morning. (Xinhua/Jiang Fan)
GYIRONG, Xizang, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Search and rescue intensified Friday at the mudslide-stricken border port of Gyirong in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region as rescue personnel raced against time to save lives.
As of 10 a.m. Friday, a total of 681 fire and rescue personnel and 113 vehicles have arrived at the remote mountainous border area, while 6,612 pieces of rescue equipment and logistical supplies have been dispatched to Gyirong Township, according to the National Fire and Rescue Administration.
The mudslide, which occurred on the Nepalese side, struck Gyirong Port in Gyirong County, Xizang, on Wednesday morning. As of 8 a.m. on Thursday, three people had been killed, 558 remained missing, while two local villagers had been rescued.
The first team of 141 rescuers, as well as a high-altitude helicopter, arrived at the port on Thursday morning. Another batch of 111 rescuers from the China Search and Rescue team reached Gyirong County Thursday afternoon.
The fire and rescue personnel have formed three specialized teams for search and rescue operations: entering by rubber boats on waterways, traveling on foot through mountainous terrain, and conducting aerial reconnaissance and supply drops with drones.
An advance team has also been sent to the core disaster area to conduct mapping, reconnaissance and targeted monitoring of both the site and the barrier lake using drones and telescopes.
A total of 13 experts from the Shanghai Fire Research Institute of the Ministry of Emergency Management have also arrived at the site.
China Anneng, a state-owned engineering and rescue enterprise, sent out a 15-member team on Friday with reconnaissance drones, portable satellite stations and mobile surveillance cameras to conduct on-site surveys of the blockage and surrounding roads to provide accurate data for efforts to address the barrier lake.
The debris accumulated about 3 km upstream of the port can only be safely cleared once the risk posed by the blockage has been resolved, according to rescue personnel at the site. ■

U.S. multi-state Cyclospora outbreak linked to iceberg lettuce tops 11,000 cases
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
17:19:37 CST
18:19:37 KST

LOS ANGELES, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- An outbreak of cyclosporiasis linked to iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico has spread to 20 states, with a total of 11,458 illnesses reported, the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) said on Thursday.
The outbreak includes people who reported exposure to processed iceberg lettuce from Taylor Farms de Mexico served or purchased at various locations, including those who previously reported eating at Taco Bell, said the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
Most cases occurred before Taylor Farms de Mexico recalled its iceberg lettuce on July 17.
The FDA said it remains confident that all recalled iceberg lettuce associated with this specific Cyclospora outbreak has been removed from the market.
The FDA's onsite inspections and sampling at iceberg lettuce growers and a processing facility in Mexico, conducted in coordination with Mexican officials, are ongoing, the agency said.
Cyclosporiasis is a gastrointestinal illness caused by the microscopic parasite Cyclospora. In the United States, infections typically increase during the spring and summer months. The CDC defines the annual cyclosporiasis surveillance season as running from May 1 through Aug. 31. ■

Norway's King Harald V dies at 89, Crown Prince Haakon succeeds to throne
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
17:19:26 CST
18:19:26 KST

People mourn King Harald V beside flowers, candles and Norwegian flags laid outside the Royal Palace in Oslo, Norway, on Aug. 28, 2026. Norway's King Harald V died at the age of 89 early Friday, the Royal House of Norway said.(Xinhua/Zhang Yuliang)
OSLO, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Norway's King Harald V died at the age of 89 early Friday, the Royal House of Norway said.
The king passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital Rikshospitalet at 6:35 a.m. local time (0435 GMT), according to a statement issued by the Royal House.
Under Norway's rules of succession, 53-year-old Crown Prince Haakon immediately succeeded to the throne and became the country's new king. His regnal name and motto have yet to be officially announced.
Harald was admitted to the hospital on Aug. 17. The Royal House previously said he had received cortisone treatment for hemolytic anemia in recent weeks, which caused fluid accumulation. During his hospitalization, he was also treated with antibiotics for a bacterial infection in his blood.
The Royal House said Thursday that Harald's health had deteriorated and his condition was "very serious."
Born on Feb. 21, 1937, Harald ascended to the throne on Jan. 17, 1991, following the death of his father, King Olav V. He had been hospitalized several times in recent years and received a permanent pacemaker in 2024.
Haakon was born on July 20, 1973. He had served as regent on multiple occasions when his father was ill or abroad. Haakon's eldest child, Princess Ingrid Alexandra, is now Norway's crown princess and the heir to the throne. ■

China sets 2030 goals for logistics network development
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
17:19:17 CST
18:19:17 KST

BEIJING, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- China has set goals to advance the development of the country's logistics network by 2030, aiming to improve connectivity and better support the real economy, according to a plan released by the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and the Ministry of Transport.
By 2030, China expects to make notable progress in developing its logistics network with closer coordination between logistics hubs and industries, enhanced internal and external connectivity, greener and smarter facilities and equipment, and greater interoperability of rules and information, according to the plan.
The plan aims to help effectively reduce logistics costs across society, bringing total social logistics costs to 13.1 percent of GDP by 2030, down 0.8 percentage points from the end of 2025.
This will help improve the efficiency and performance of the real economy and support smoother economic circulation and high-quality development, it said.
The plan outlines 17 key tasks in seven areas, including advancing the development and connectivity of logistics hubs, enhancing the capacity of logistics corridors, addressing shortcomings in urban and rural logistics facilities, and promoting the digitalization, smart development and green transformation of logistics facilities and equipment.
The logistics network is one of the six networks prioritized during China's 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), alongside water networks, new-type power grids, computing power networks, next-generation communication networks and urban underground pipeline networks.
The NDRC has described the six networks as an integrated whole featuring deep interconnection, mutual empowerment and coordinated support. Investment in the six networks and key areas is preliminarily estimated to exceed 7 trillion yuan (about 1.03 trillion U.S. dollars) this year. ■

Malaysia eyes 12.4 bln USD in medical devices exports by 2030

KUALA LUMPUR, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- Malaysia is working to realize 50 billion ringgit (about 12.4 billion U.S. dollars) in medical device exports by 2030 by developing technology, owning intellectual property, and building world-class medical technology companies, Deputy Prime Minister Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said on Friday.
Citing the sector's successful growth, which generated 34.54 billion ringgit in exports in 2025, Zahid said during the closing ceremony of the KLCC International Medical Device Exhibition and Conference 2026.
"We have the foundations for manufacturing, market access and global confidence. However, the next stage of our export growth needs to be increasingly driven by high-value products," he said.
Zahid explained the success of the sector should be measured not only by the amount of foreign capital inflow or the number of products manufactured in Malaysia but also by the number of Malaysian medical technology companies capable of competing regionally and globally, with the government having set a target for the development of at least 10 such companies.
"We must also look at the amount of intellectual property and technology being developed here, as well as the number of Malaysian companies that become global players," he said.
He noted that by 2025, roughly 4 billion ringgit in new investments in the medical devices sector had been approved through 46 projects, creating nearly 3,400 jobs, adding that the medical technology industry must work proactively with universities and technical, vocational education, and training institutions to ensure a capable workforce is ready before investments arrive. France's CPI to rise 2.4 pct in August
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
17:19:03 CST
18:19:03 KST

PARIS, Aug. 28 (Xinhua) -- France's consumer price index (CPI) is expected to rise 2.4 percent year on year in August, up from 2.1 percent in July, according to preliminary data released on Friday by the National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE).
In its provisional estimate, INSEE said the acceleration in inflation was mainly driven by faster increases in energy prices, particularly petroleum products.
The year-on-year decline in manufactured goods prices was expected to narrow further, while food prices were projected to increase slightly faster. By contrast, service prices are expected to slow slightly, while tobacco prices are projected to rise at the same pace as in July.
On a monthly basis, consumer prices were expected to increase 0.7 percent in August, following a 0.6-percent rise in July. The increase was mainly attributed to the seasonal rebound in manufactured goods prices, particularly clothing and footwear, following declines during the summer sales in July.
Energy prices were also expected to rise again, driven by higher petroleum product prices, while food prices, particularly fresh produce, were projected to increase. Service and tobacco prices were expected to remain stable from the previous month.
The Harmonised Index of Consumer Prices, used for comparisons across the eurozone, was expected to rise 2.7 percent year on year in August, up from 2.4 percent in July. ■

====================================================================================================

UK troops to trial foot-launched military paragliders
United Kingdom
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
10:18:34 BST
18:18:34 KST

British troops are preparing to trial a new foot-launched military paraglider developed by Wiltshire-based start-up Blakcro with around £6 million in Ministry of Defence support, the UK Defence Journal understands.
The Ministry of Defence said on 28 August that the system has been designed to allow an individual operator to launch without a runway, helicopter or transport aircraft, with the Royal Marines and Parachute Regiment expected to trial the concept in the coming months.
Blakcro has developed the system with support from UK Defence Innovation, or UKDI, which acts as an entry point into defence for companies that have not previously worked with the Ministry of Defence. The company is supplying systems during 2026 and into 2027.
According to the MOD, the aircraft can be packed into a case approximately the size of a large rucksack and assembled in under eight minutes, including in darkness. The department also says it has been designed with reduced acoustic, visual and radar signatures for use during covert insertions.
The system is built around a UK-made titanium airframe and, according to the MOD, can travel up to 200 miles under its own power. It has also been designed to accommodate equipment including body armour, night-vision devices and weapon mounts.
The MOD said the technology is already in operational use and that Blakcro holds contracts in the UK and with NATO allies. The planned Royal Marines and Parachute Regiment activity would examine the concept as a means of individual air mobility for British forces.
Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry Luke Pollard said in the release: “With UK Defence Innovation supporting SMEs like Blakcro from the drawing board through to deployment, we are building a more resilient, homegrown defence supply chain and ensuring our armed forces receive the pioneering equipment that can give them the edge on the battlefield.”
He added: “Defence has a new way of working with industry, backing British innovation to deliver cutting-edge capability for our armed forces and good jobs in regions like Wiltshire.”
Blakcro first engaged with UKDI through its Open Call for Innovation and has since received support across two other projects. One of those projects received a Defence Innovation Loan, which the MOD said helped the company move from development of a single product into full production.
The company has grown from three employees to 11 since receiving UKDI support and now holds three prime contracts involving the UK and NATO allies, according to the department.
Sam Wedgwood, founder and chief executive of Blakcro, said in the release: “From a UKDI success story perspective, we have very rapidly moved from base technology in 2024, through UKDI-supported rapid innovation, through to purchase, through to operational use by 2026.”
Wedgwood added: “We could not have done that at this pace without the support we have received – not just the funding, but the commercialisation support and the access to the right people. UKDI kept telling us we were special. I think it’s mutual.”
The concept differs from conventional military parachuting and air assault methods by giving the individual operator a self-contained means of getting airborne from the ground. A pilot launches the system on foot rather than from an aircraft, while propulsion provides sustained powered flight after take-off.
The MOD is presenting the programme as part of a wider effort to bring smaller UK companies into defence procurement and accelerate technologies from early development into operational use. For Blakcro, the next stage will include the planned trials with the Royal Marines and Parachute Regiment as the services assess how the system could be used in practice.

Glacier collapse in Nepal may have caused disaster, says China amid concern over 'overflowing' barrier lake
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:17:43 UTC
18:17:43 KST

Riyaz ul Khaliq
28 August 2026•Update: 28 August 2026
- Fresh concerns as large barrier lake formed amid flash floods 'reportedly breaches'
 
China on Friday suggested that the collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal may have triggered the disaster across the border, which killed at least 480 people, as President Xi Jinping pressed officials to make "every effort" to search for all missing Chinese and foreign nationals.
"We noted that experts and official institutions of China and Nepal have made preliminary assessment on the cause of the disaster," Foreign Ministry spokesman Lin Jian told reporters in Beijing when asked about the Wednesday morning flash floods that hit northern and central Nepal as well as China’s southern Tibet region.
The floods and landslides struck northern and central Nepal early Wednesday, sweeping through communities along the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers and carrying people and debris downstream.
On the Chinese side of the border, mudslides hit Gyirong County in the southwestern Xizang Autonomous Region, also known as Tibet.
"The disaster may have been triggered by a collapse of a high-altitude glacier in Nepal," Lin said.
The statement came from Beijing as the death toll from devastating flash floods rose to 480, with more than 1,200 people, most of them foreign nationals, still missing.
The Nepalese police said the death toll from Wednesday's floods had reached 475, while China has confirmed five deaths.
 
Barrier lake reportedly breaches
On Friday, fresh concerns were raised after a large barrier lake that formed amid the flash floods reportedly breached, "raising fresh concerns of another surge of water into Nepal’s Bhotekoshi river," the daily Kathmandu Post reported.
Beijing had warned on Thursday that the lake near the confluence of the Chhochen Khola and Purepu Tsangpo rivers was "already overflowing" and posed a “high risk of a breach.”
The two rivers merge before entering Nepal, where the river is known as Bhotekoshi, the main tributary of the Trishuli River.
"Information has come that the lake on the Chinese side has breached. So, preparations are underway to send helicopters stationed in Dhunche and Rasuwa for reconnaissance," said a rescue official at Nepal's Tribhuvan International Airport.
Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the water level in the Bhotekoshi River has surged, warning of possible additional floods.
However, Nepal's Education Minister Sasmita Pokharel said there "is no immediate major risk," according to the Online Khabar outlet.
The Foreign Ministry in Kathmandu said 596 people from 33 countries were still missing.
Another 127 Nepalese nationals were unaccounted for, according to the Nepal Tourism Board.
China said 558 people, including 260 foreigners, remained missing in Tibet as search-and-rescue operations continued.
Figures shared by Nepal and China showed that some 1,281 people, including 856 foreigners, were still missing.
Lin said the details of the foreigners missing "are being verified" and that Beijing "has already notified relevant countries’ embassies."
Leaders of the ruling Communist Party of China met in Beijing on Friday under President Xi and emphasized that: "All relevant authorities and departments must take resolute and effective measures for the rescue-related work."
"China will provide emergency aid to the disaster-hit area in Nepal and carry out international rescue cooperation," the meeting said, according to state-run Xinhua News.
The water surge on Wednesday led to flooding in the Bhotekoshi River in Rasuwa, northern Nepal, while flash floods and mudslides swept through the Timure and Syaphrubesi areas, causing widespread devastation before the floodwaters flowed downstream toward the Trishuli River.

Drone Attack Kills One, Sparks Fire at Yaroslavl Oil Refinery
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:17:25 UTC
18:17:25 KST

A Ukrainian drone attack killed one person and sparked a fire at one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in the city of Yaroslavl, Russian and Ukrainian authorities said Friday.
Yaroslavl region Governor Mikhail Yevrayev said one civilian was killed and 27 others were injured after falling drone debris hit an intercity bus.
He claimed that 67 Ukrainian drones were downed over the region, but that drone debris fell on residential areas, commercial properties and “industrial infrastructure.”
Ukraine’s military said it struck the Slavneft-Yanos refinery, which it said provides fuel and lubricants for the Russian military. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky later confirmed the attack and added that Ukraine’s SBU security service had struck a Tu-95MS missile-carrying aircraft in the Saratov region city of Engels.
Independent reports said that Ukrainian drones had already attacked Slavneft-Yanos at least seven times this year before Friday’s attack.
In the Moscow region town of Pavlovsky Posad, a drone slammed into a Magnit grocery store, blowing out windows at a neighboring clinic. Governor Andrei Vorobyov said the clinic remained open despite the damage.
Separate Ukrainian attacks in the southwestern Belgorod region killed two people and injured nine others over the last 24 hours, according to the local governor.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 512 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Thursday night and Friday morning.

Baltic Sea nations plan drone defence task force, Germany says
FLENSBURG, Germany, Aug 28 - The countries bordering the Baltic Sea plan to establish a joint task force for drone defence that will allow them to react quickly in the face of the growing threat of hybrid attacks, said German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt on Friday.
Numerous incidents of possible sabotage affecting undersea cables and critical gas pipelines have taken place in the Baltic Sea, bordered by eight NATO countries and Russia, since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion in Ukraine in 2022.
The goal is to set up a task force that allows quick information exchange, said Dobrindt ahead of a meeting in the northern German city of Flensburg with his Baltic Sea counterparts.
"Foreign powers attempt daily to attack and undermine democracy, security and economic strength within the EU," said the interior minister in a statement on the meeting's objective.
He warned that such attacks could "take on a new dimension in the coming months" and the hybrid threat is "omnipresent."
Germany has been particularly on alert over drone threats after one carrying explosives was found at Leipzig/Halle Airport - an important military logistics hub - earlier this month.
German officials have not publicly blamed any foreign countries for the incident, though some lawmakers have pointed their finger at Russia, which has dismissed the incident as "fabricated provocation." REUTERS

Türkiye’s economic confidence rises above key threshold in August

Türkiye’s economic confidence index rose above the 100-point threshold in August, official data showed Friday.
The index increased 0.8% from the previous month to 100.6, up from 99.8 in July, according to the Turkish Statistical Institute (TurkStat).
A reading above 100 indicates optimism regarding the overall economic outlook, while a figure below the threshold signals pessimism.
The improvement was driven by higher confidence among consumers and manufacturers.
The consumer confidence index rose 1% month-on-month to 90.8, while the real sector confidence index for the manufacturing industry climbed 1.2% to 102.4.
Confidence weakened modestly across the services, retail trade and construction sectors.
The services confidence index edged down 0.1% to 111.9, while retail trade confidence fell 0.8% to 110.1.
The construction confidence index declined 0.4% to 83.1, remaining the weakest among the sectoral indicators.

A program focusing on Turkish television series’ contribution to Türkiye’s global brand began in Istanbul on Friday, bringing together senior officials and representatives of the industry.
The event, The Global Narrative of the Türkiye Brand: Turkish TV Series, was organized by Türkiye’s Communications Directorate.
Türkiye’s Head of Communications Burhanettin Duran said Turkish productions reach more than 1 billion viewers in over 170 countries, while the country ranks among the world’s top three TV series exporters.
Türkiye’s TV series exports, which stood at about $10 million in the early 2000s, have now exceeded $1 billion, Duran said.
“When a Turkish series reaches a family in Damascus, a living room in Rabat, a home in Belgrade or a viewer in Santiago or Johannesburg, Türkiye ceases to be a distant country seen only on a map,” he added.

The revised system also allows multiple projects from the same production company to receive support.

Facade of Justice Palace visible for first time in 40 years (video)
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-28
09:06:29 UTC
18:06:29 KST

It’s a moment we thought would never happen: The scaffolding has been removed from the front of Brussels’ iconic Justice Palace, revealing the beautifully renovated facade. Scaffolding on other parts of the building will remain in place as renovations continue for the next 14 years.
It’s worthy of a parade and yet it was done without fanfare: Scaffolding was removed from the Justice Palace in Brussels this week, revealing the facade of the building for the first time in more than 40 years. The scaffolding was placed in the 1980s not because works were ready to get started on the 143-year old building but in order to stabilise the crumbling exterior.
“I’m glad that we can see this success,” said federal justice minister Annelies Verlinden (CD&V), “which offers hope and perspective for the future of this building and – by extension – for the justice department.”
Aside from criticism from within the justice system regarding chronic underfunding, the minister is referring to the long and confused history of the renovations to the Justice Palace, one of the world’s largest courthouses. Anyone who has lived in Brussels for less than 40 years had never seen the building without its telltale scaffolding.
Renovations have since the 1980s gone along in fits and starts, mired in political red tape. The regional and federal governments could not agree on who should foot the bill, which at this point is more than €600 million in total for the exterior and interior. There was also ongoing discussions about whether all or part of the building should be repurposed, which would have a major impact on renovations to the dilapidated interior portions.
The complexity of the renovations to this heritage monument has also led to problems getting started – made worse as key renovations are continually delayed. In fact, when a new renovation plan was launched in 2021, the first urgent renovations to be carried out were on the scaffolding itself.
The Justice Palace
- Designed by architect Joseph Poelaert and completed in 1883
- Upon completion, it was the largest building in Europe and the largest courthouse in the world
- At 26,000 square metres (not including parking), it is still one of the largest courthouses in the world
- It is aligned on the same axis as the Royal Palace and federal parliament, a symbolic straight line connecting the three powers of the state: executive, legislative and judicial
While every decade has brought announcements and expectations for the building, including the completion of key works to the roof and full renovation of the magnificent dome, things really only started moving in the right direction a few years ago when it was decided that the federal government was responsible for funding, planning and monitoring the works.
Along with the front facade, the steps and exterior entryway have also been renovated. The fencing around the forecourt has been replaced – an exact replica of the original that was designed in 1883.
The second phase of the plan includes the renovations of the base of the dome (still covered in scaffolding). This is scheduled to complete in 2030. Following that will be renovations to the other exterior facades of the building so that the entire exterior is complete by 2035.
The public should access the justice system in a building where the appearance reflects the dignity of this system
Justice minister Annelies Verlinden
Only then will improvements the interior will be tackled. The walls, floors, ceilings and outstanding architectural elements have been severely damaged over the decades because of moisture and leakage. Parts of ceilings have collapsed over the years, and chunks of plaster and stone have fallen to the ground. The building is also home to birds, rats and mice.
“It is my firm ambition that everyone who works in the justice system can do so in a modern, comfortable environment,” said Verlinden. “Equally, members of the public should be able to access the justice system in a building where the appearance reflects the dignity of this system.”
Works to the interior of the building will follow complete of exterior renovations. The entire project is meant to finish by 2040.
